name: Yellowstone
hook: The world's first national park — and the geysers, Wyoming and Grand Teton clues it keeps generating.

facts.label: the first national park
facts.statement: It became the world's first national park in 1872, when President Ulysses S. Grant signed the law; in 1978 it was among the first 12 UNESCO World Heritage sites.

facts.label: Mi tse a-da-zi
facts.statement: The name comes from the Yellowstone River; Native people called it Mi tse a-da-zi, which French trappers translated as "Pierre Jaune" — yellow stone.

facts.label: Old Faithful
facts.statement: Old Faithful erupts about every 90 minutes, throwing some 5,000 gallons; at least 120 of the park's geysers have names, including Giant and Clepsydra.

facts.label: Wyoming, Montana and Idaho
facts.statement: The park lies mostly in Wyoming's northwest corner and spills over into Montana and Idaho.

facts.label: Grand Teton National Park
facts.statement: Grand Teton National Park, just south of Yellowstone, is the only national park entirely inside Wyoming.

facts.label: John Colter
facts.statement: John Colter explored the region around 1807 after leaving the Lewis and Clark expedition, and was among the first white men to describe its wonders.

facts.label: geysers and hot springs
facts.statement: Yellowstone holds roughly half the world's geysers, plus hot springs where heat-loving Archaea thrive in places like Octopus Spring.
